facts.text: Hidden Springs is a master‑planned community established in 1987 in the Dry Creek Valley of Ada County, Idaho.
The community preserves more than 800 acres of open space and runs its own wastewater treatment facility.
Hidden Springs’ historic Farmstead, one of Idaho’s oldest intact farmhouses, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its farming heritage.
The area’s agricultural roots are highlighted by the preserved Farmstead, which still raises chickens, honey bees, and herbs.
Elevations in Hidden Springs range from about 2,560 feet at the valley mouth to 2,950 feet at foothill crests, creating gently undulating terrain.
Euro‑American settlement began in the early 1860s after gold discoveries in the Boise Basin, prompting supply farms to feed miners and troops.
